reality_delta: The main claim reports one failure mode and two direct timing measurements, but it has not yet shown that ~59 s is a stable, acceptable baseline. The proposed change will alter a timeout constant, yet the calibration rationale remains anecdotal rather than measured.
main_concern: Raising the child timeout from 45 s to just above a single observed ~59 s run risks treating a symptom as calibration and may bypass a legitimate performance signal if the package enforcement check has become too slow.
top_risks: Statistical insignificance: one package run (59.2 s) and one source run (63.2 s) do not establish a p95/p99; the new timeout could still false-fail under normal variance or pass under a real regression.

Outer/child timeout mismatch: without documented outer-timeout values and margin, a child timeout set too close to the outer boundary can be killed by the parent anyway, rendering the child raise ineffective.
Self-check fragility: a regression guard based on wall-clock duration can become flaky or be tuned upward to silence failures, gradually weakening strict checking.
missing_evidence: Repeated timing measurements of both package and source enforcement-check under CI/E2E-like conditions (mean, p95, variance).
A rationale or profile showing where the ~60 s is spent, to prove it is expected and not a performance regression.
Current values and nesting of all related timeouts (outer package check, child prism check, E2E step timeout) and the intended margin between them.
minimum_fix: Before raising the timeout: gather multiple CI-like runs to establish a stable upper-bound duration; set the child timeout to p95 + a fixed margin (e.g., 20–30%) and enforce child_timeout + overhead < outer_timeout; add a separate telemetry/assert that records direct enforcement-check duration and fails if it exceeds a distinct performance budget, so calibration cannot silently regress.

anti_loop_signal.reason: Reject any follow-up that only says 'we raised it above the measured time' without quantified variance, documented outer-timeout margin, and a distinct performance guard.

user_intent_alignment: Aligned only if the timeout raise prevents killing a healthy check that normally takes ~60 s. Misaligned if it allows a legitimately degraded/slow check to pass, because Norven wants real RedCap mechanism failures exposed, not hidden by a looser timeout.
